outlines.version: Skills measured as of November 16, 2026 (only version shown; page updated 2026-10-21)

domains.title: Plan AI-powered business solutions
Design AI-powered business solutions
Deploy AI-powered business solutions

articles.title: AI vs ML vs Deep Learning vs Generative AI vs Agentic AI
articles.scope: Defines each layer of the AI stack and contrasts them by data needs, outputs, determinism and explainability. Covers GenAI advantages (adaptability, responsiveness) and disadvantages (hallucination, interpretability, inaccuracy, nondeterminism), the use-case catalog, and when traditional ML beats a foundation model or AI is the wrong tool. Agentic depth links to ai/agents.

articles.title: Learning Paradigms and ML Tasks: Supervised, Unsupervised, Self-Supervised and Reinforcement
articles.scope: Contrasts the four paradigms by where the training signal comes from, plus labeled vs unlabeled data. Maps tasks (classification, regression, clustering, anomaly detection, forecasting, recommendation, dimensionality reduction) to baseline algorithms, with depth in ml-algorithms-reference. Shows LLM pre-training is self-supervised while RLHF and RFT are reinforcement learning.

articles.title: Classic ML Algorithms Field Guide: Linear Models, Trees and Boosting, k-NN, Clustering, Anomaly Detection, Forecasting and Recommenders
articles.scope: For each algorithm family gives task, data shape, interpretability, scaling and failure modes. Maps each to SageMaker AI built-ins (XGBoost, LightGBM, CatBoost, AutoGluon-Tabular, TabTransformer, Linear Learner, k-NN, Factorization Machines, k-means, PCA, Random Cut Forest, IP Insights, DeepAR, Object2Vec, BlazingText, Seq2Seq, LDA, NTM, vision algorithms) and to Azure ML automated ML task types.

articles.title: The ML Lifecycle: From Data to Training to Inference
articles.scope: Walks framing, collection, EDA, preparation, training, evaluation, deployment, monitoring and retraining, and catalogs data types (labeled/unlabeled, tabular, time-series, image, text, structured/unstructured). Contrasts training with inference, covers the FM lifecycle, FM sources and managed-API vs self-hosted use. Azure ML and SageMaker AI tabs link to ai/platforms.

articles.title: Data for ML: Formats, Batch vs Streaming Ingestion, Storage Choices and Training-Data Access
articles.scope: Compares formats (Parquet, ORC, Avro, JSON, CSV, RecordIO) by access pattern and batch vs streaming ingestion (Kinesis, Data Firehose, Managed Service for Apache Flink, Kafka, Event Hubs). Covers storage trade-offs (S3, EFS, FSx, EBS, Blob/ADLS), merging sources with Glue or Spark, Azure ML datastores and data assets, and capacity troubleshooting. Links data/row-vs-columnar-storage and cloud/*/storage-data.

articles.title: Data Preparation and Feature Engineering for ML
articles.scope: Covers cleaning, scaling vs standardization, binning, encodings (one-hot, label, binary, tokenization), labeling (Ground Truth, Mechanical Turk, Azure ML data labeling), class imbalance and pre-training bias metrics, resampling and synthetic data, splits and leakage, data quality (Glue DataBrew/Data Quality) and feature stores with a packaged feature retrieval spec. Python and C# (ML.NET) code; data protection links to security/data-protection.

articles.title: Overfitting vs Underfitting and the Bias-Variance Trade-off
articles.scope: Explains fit and generalization with learning curves, contrasting symptoms and fixes (more data, regularization, dropout, early stopping, capacity, cross-validation). Distinguishes statistical bias from algorithmic bias and from catastrophic forgetting, so the reader can diagnose a model from its curves.

articles.title: Training Mechanics: Loss, Gradient Descent, Hyperparameters and Distributed Training
articles.scope: Explains loss, gradient descent, learning rate, epochs, steps and batch size, regularization, early stopping and convergence debugging (SageMaker Debugger). Covers tuning (SageMaker AMT vs Azure ML sweep jobs), AutoML, ensembling and stacking, script mode and external models, and data- vs model-parallel distributed training on both clouds.

articles.title: ML Evaluation Metrics: Classification, Regression and Ranking
articles.scope: Reference for confusion matrix, accuracy, precision, recall, F1, ROC-AUC, PR-AUC, log loss, MAE/RMSE/R2, thresholds and baselines, plus ranking metrics (precision@k, recall@k, MRR, nDCG) reused for retrieval. Shows when each misleads and ties model metrics to business metrics.

articles.title: From Neural Networks to Transformers: How LLMs Generate Text
articles.scope: Opens with a foundation-level summary, then builds from neurons and backpropagation through CNNs and RNNs to transformers: tokenization, embeddings, self-attention, encoder-only vs decoder-only vs encoder-decoder, next-token prediction. Practitioner depth covers KV cache, prefill vs decode and mixture-of-experts, explaining hallucination, nondeterminism, latency and cost.

articles.title: Tokens, Embeddings and Context Windows
articles.scope: Contrasts tokens (processing, quota and billing unit) with embeddings, shows tokenizers differ by model with C# and Python counting, and budgets the context window across system prompt, history, retrieval, tools, hidden reasoning and output, including truncation and lost-in-the-middle.

articles.title: Inference Parameters: Temperature, Top-p, Top-k, Penalties, Reasoning Effort and Output Limits
articles.scope: Reference for temperature, top-p, top-k, penalties, max output tokens, stop sequences, seed, reasoning effort and service_tier, including which reasoning models reject. Compares three request shapes: OpenAI-style Responses/Chat Completions (Foundry, and Bedrock bedrock-runtime and bedrock-mantle endpoints), Bedrock Converse (inferenceConfig plus additionalModelRequestFields such as top_k) and InvokeModel.

articles.title: Choosing a Model: Frontier vs Small, Open-Weight vs Proprietary, Multimodal and Reasoning
articles.scope: Selection framework weighing capability, modality, context, latency, price, prompt-caching support, licensing (open-weight vs open-source), residency, fine-tunability, tool support and remaining lifecycle. Covers when a small or customized model wins, reading benchmarks (contamination, saturation) and confirming with own evals, and keeping model switches cheap.

articles.title: Multimodal and Generative Media Models: Vision-Language, Diffusion and Speech
articles.scope: Contrasts vision-language models, diffusion image and video generators, and speech models (STT, TTS, native speech-to-speech) by mechanism, inputs and outputs, and why they are hard to evaluate. Implementation lives in the applied vision and speech pages; provenance and multimodal safety link to security/ai-security.

articles.title: AI Workloads Map: Text Analysis, Speech, Vision, Information Extraction and Generation
articles.scope: Catalogs workloads and contrasts purpose-built services with LLM prompting for each. Orients on Azure Language, Translator, Speech, Vision, Document Intelligence and Content Understanding (each in Foundry Tools) versus Amazon Comprehend, Translate, Transcribe, Polly, Lex, Rekognition, Textract and Bedrock Data Automation, linking to ai/platforms and the applied pages.

articles.title: Responsible AI Principles: From Values to Design Decisions
articles.scope: Teaches recurring principles (fairness, reliability and safety, privacy and security, inclusiveness, transparency, accountability, explainability, controllability, veracity and robustness, governance) as design consequences, introducing Microsoft's six principles and AWS's eight dimensions as two framings. Covers model cards, Transparency Notes, AI Service Cards, human oversight, environmental and legal risks; the mapping lives in cloud/compare and governance in security/ai-security.

articles.title: Explainability, Fairness and Bias Measurement in Practice
articles.scope: Contrasts interpretability with post-hoc explainability (SHAP, feature importance, counterfactuals), defines fairness metrics, selection vs measurement bias and pre- vs post-training bias metrics, and evaluates models against responsible AI principles. Uses the Azure ML Responsible AI dashboard vs SageMaker Clarify and covers LLM-era transparency (citations, confidence).

articles.title: Calling Models from Code: Messages, Roles, Streaming, Stop Reasons, Usage Accounting and Conversation State
articles.scope: Explains roles, content parts, streaming events, finish reasons, usage fields (input, output, cached, cache-write, reasoning tokens) and stateless vs server-side state. Contrasts Responses, Chat Completions and Bedrock Converse/InvokeModel including Bedrock's OpenAI-compatible endpoints, Foundry projects, instant access and keyless auth, with C# and Python samples.

articles.title: Prompt Engineering: From Zero-Shot to Chain-of-Thought
articles.scope: Covers roles, context, instructions, delimiters, zero/one/few-shot, chain-of-thought and self-consistency, templates, chaining, negative prompts and organization-wide prompt guidelines. Risks (exposure, poisoning, hijacking, jailbreaking) link to security/ai-security; C# and Python on Foundry and Bedrock.

articles.title: Context Engineering: Deciding What the Model Sees
articles.scope: Treats the window as a budget: instruction hierarchy, history compression, retrieved evidence, tool results, memory, ordering and lost-in-the-middle, pruning, prompt compression, and stable prefixes for cache hits. Agent memory links to ai/agents.

articles.title: Hallucinations and Grounding: Causes, Detection and Mitigation
articles.scope: Explains why models fabricate and contrasts grounding (RAG, tool results, citations, abstention, schema output, text-to-SQL) with detection (groundedness evaluation, logprob confidence, consistency checks, verification passes). Provider guardrail checks are owned by security/ai-security.

articles.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation End to End
articles.scope: Reference architecture from grounding-data review through ingestion, parsing, chunking, embedding, indexing, retrieval, reranking, prompt assembly, cited generation and evaluation, with failure modes per stage. Tabs orient on Azure AI Search knowledge bases (Foundry IQ as managed permission-aware layer) and Bedrock Knowledge Bases, warning that 'knowledge base' differs per cloud.

articles.title: Document Ingestion and Chunking Strategies
articles.scope: Compares parsers (text, OCR, layout-aware, multimodal, Content Understanding markdown) and chunking (fixed with overlap, sentence, semantic, heading-aware, hierarchical, none). Covers metadata enrichment, validation before embedding (Glue Data Quality), multimodal content, and the precision vs completeness trade-off of chunk size.

articles.title: Embedding Models and Vector Indexes
articles.scope: Covers embedding choice (dimensions, domain, multilingual, Matryoshka) and fine-tuning with contrastive pairs and hard negatives; metrics, HNSW/IVF/DiskANN, quantization and binary vectors, pre- vs post-filtering (pgvector 0.8+ iterative scans). Orients on Azure AI Search, Cosmos DB for NoSQL, Azure DocumentDB, PostgreSQL pgvector, Azure SQL vector type, Managed Redis, OpenSearch, Aurora/RDS pgvector, Neptune Analytics, S3 Vectors and third-party stores.

articles.title: Vector vs Keyword vs Hybrid Search, and Reranking
articles.scope: Contrasts BM25 full-text, dense vector, learned sparse and hybrid search with reciprocal rank fusion, then cross-encoder reranking (Azure semantic ranker vs Bedrock rerankers), the 'semantic search' naming trap, and tuning thresholds and top-k.

articles.title: Advanced RAG Patterns: Query Transformation, Agentic Retrieval and Long Context
articles.scope: Catalogs rewriting, decomposition, HyDE, small-to-big retrieval, multimodal RAG and agentic retrieval; on Azure, knowledge bases with reasoning effort minimal/low/medium (REST 2026-04-01 GA minimal extractive; 2026-08-01-preview planning and answer synthesis) and an MCP endpoint. Covers RAG vs long-context and cache-augmented generation, freshness and security trimming, with cost and latency trade-offs.

articles.title: GraphRAG vs Vector RAG
articles.scope: Explains entity extraction, community summaries and traversal, contrasting GraphRAG with vector RAG on multi-hop questions, indexing cost and upkeep. Compares Microsoft's self-run open-source GraphRAG with managed Bedrock Knowledge Bases GraphRAG (vector search then Neptune Analytics traversal; S3 only; no graph-build customization; 1,000 files per source default; child chunks only).

articles.title: Grounding on Structured Data: Text-to-SQL, Semantic Layers and Knowledge Bases over Databases
articles.scope: Contrasts vector RAG with SQL generation for exact aggregates; covers schema linking, semantic layers, curated views, example queries and execution-accuracy evaluation, plus read-only roles, allow-lists, timeouts and row-level security. Tabs cover Bedrock Knowledge Bases over structured stores and Azure equivalents.

articles.title: Intelligent Document Processing: Purpose-Built Analyzers vs Generative Extraction
articles.scope: Builds pipelines combining OCR, layout, classification, segmentation and field extraction into grounded markdown for RAG or schema JSON with confidence scores. Contrasts Content Understanding analyzers, Document Intelligence, Textract and Bedrock Data Automation with structured-output extraction; covers human review (Amazon A2I), field-level precision/recall and audio/video extraction.

articles.title: Vision Applications: Captioning, Visual Q&A, Alt-Text, Object Detection, and Image and Video Generation
articles.scope: Implements captions, visually grounded Q&A, accessibility alt-text, video-segment analysis and object/region identification with multimodal models and Content Understanding single-task and pro-mode pipelines. Implements generation from prompts and reference media, inpainting, mask edits and video editing across Foundry, Bedrock and Rekognition; multimodal safety links to security/ai-security.

articles.title: Speech and Voice: Cascaded STT-LLM-TTS Pipelines vs Native Speech-to-Speech Models
articles.scope: Contrasts cascaded pipelines with realtime speech-to-speech models on latency, turn detection, barge-in, tone, control and cost. Covers speech as an agent modality, custom speech, audio reasoning, speech translation and WER, comparing Azure Speech in Foundry Tools and Foundry realtime models with Transcribe, Polly, Lex and Bedrock speech models.

articles.title: Text Analysis: LLM Prompting vs Purpose-Built Language Services
articles.scope: Contrasts prompting with Azure Language, CLU and Translator in Foundry Tools and Amazon Comprehend and Translate for entities, topics, summaries, sentiment, safety, PII, translation and JSON output. Gives criteria (cost per record, determinism, latency, languages, PII guarantees, customization) and enrichment-before-prompting patterns.

articles.title: Prompting vs RAG vs Fine-Tuning vs Distillation vs Custom Models vs Pre-Training
articles.scope: Compares what each approach changes, data needed, training, hosting and per-token cost, and effect on freshness, latency and risk, including combined approaches and build-buy-extend. The reader can defend a customization choice in an architecture review.

articles.title: Fine-Tuning Methods: SFT, Continued Pre-Training, LoRA and Full Fine-Tuning
articles.scope: Explains SFT, continued (continuous) pre-training, transfer learning, PEFT/LoRA vs full fine-tuning, data prep, hyperparameters and forgetting. Foundry: managed fine-tuning vs interactive training (preview), training types (Standard, Data zone, Global, Developer), serving via serverless types, managed compute LoRA (preview) or Fireworks. Bedrock: SFT, RFT, distillation, Provisioned Throughput or on-demand custom deployment, Legacy limits.

articles.title: Alignment and Preference Tuning: RLHF vs DPO vs Reinforcement Fine-Tuning
articles.scope: Contrasts RLHF, DPO and RFT with graders or reward functions: data needs, reward hacking and grader testing on correct, incorrect and adversarial answers. Maps Foundry model-specific DPO and RFT and Bedrock RFT with Lambda reward functions (no DPO).

articles.title: Making Models Smaller: Distillation, Quantization, Pruning and Synthetic Data
articles.scope: Contrasts teacher-student distillation with quantization and pruning, and generates and validates synthetic data for training, rebalancing and evaluation. Covers Bedrock managed distillation and Foundry distillation via teacher-generated SFT data, and when a small model beats a frontier one.

articles.title: GenAI Integration Patterns: Sync, Streaming, Async, Batch and Event-Driven
articles.scope: Wires models into apps: sync calls, SSE/WebSocket/SignalR streaming, queue-based async (Service Bus, SQS), event-driven enrichment (Event Grid, EventBridge), Functions or Lambda APIs, batch, backoff, idempotency, degradation and OpenTelemetry across hops. C# and Python; transport links to messaging/.

articles.title: Multitenant GenAI and RAG: Isolating Indexes, Prompts, Caches, Quotas and Costs per Tenant
articles.scope: Compares index-per-tenant, shared index with security filters and hybrid isolation; isolates prompts, memory and caches (prompt_cache_key partitioning). Covers RBAC on models, grounding and tuning data, per-tenant quotas and chargeback at a gateway, and noisy-neighbor control on provisioned capacity; the threat model lives in security/ai-security.

articles.title: GenAI Solution Architecture: From Use Case and PoC to Production Reference Architectures
articles.scope: Takes a use case through a PoC testing feasibility, performance and value to standardized production components. Presents two-cloud architectures for chat over data, document processing, batch enrichment, copilots and agent-backed workflows, with build-buy-extend; Well-Architected lens content stays in architecture/well-architected.

articles.title: Evaluating GenAI Systems: Offline vs Online, Reference-Based vs Reference-Free
articles.scope: Frames evaluation across selection, pre-production and production; covers golden, synthetic and adversarial sets with data mapping, risk and safety evaluations, validation criteria for custom models, variance and sample size, human evaluation and CI quality gates. Red teaming links to security/ai-security.

articles.title: GenAI Quality and Safety Metrics Reference
articles.scope: Reference for groundedness, relevance, coherence, fluency, similarity, completeness, F1/exact match, BLEU, ROUGE, METEOR, BERTScore, WER, safety and business-alignment metrics, each with rubric, thresholds, pitfalls and matching Foundry evaluator or Bedrock metric.

articles.title: LLM-as-a-Judge: Rubrics, Biases and Calibration
articles.scope: Designs judge prompts and rubrics (pointwise vs pairwise, scored vs binary), mitigates position, verbosity and self-preference bias, calibrates against human labels with agreement statistics and controls judge cost, using Foundry custom evaluators and Bedrock LLM-as-a-judge jobs.

articles.title: Evaluating RAG: Retrieval Metrics vs Answer Metrics
articles.scope: Separates retrieval quality (recall@k, precision@k, MRR, nDCG, context precision and recall) from answer quality (groundedness, relevance, completeness, citation accuracy); builds a RAG test set and A/B-tests chunking, embeddings and thresholds with Foundry and Bedrock RAG evaluations.

articles.title: Human Feedback in Production: Ratings, Annotation Queues and Turning Feedback into Evals
articles.scope: Designs feedback capture, sampling, annotation queues, labeling guidelines, approval steps and inter-annotator agreement; covers privacy of captured content, backlog analysis and promoting reviewed cases into golden datasets, with Bedrock human-based evaluation and Amazon A2I as managed options.

articles.title: Online Experiments for ML and GenAI: A/B Tests, Canaries, Shadow Traffic and Significance
articles.scope: Contrasts A/B, canary, shadow and interleaving; covers power, sample size, guardrail metrics and stopping rules. Maps SageMaker AI production and shadow variants, Azure ML online endpoint traffic split and mirroring, gateway prompt/model variants and Bedrock Flows aliases.

articles.title: MLOps: Experiment Tracking, Model Registry, Pipelines and CI/CD/CT
articles.scope: Covers workspaces, datastores, compute targets, environments, components, registries, MLflow tracking and lineage, orchestrator choice (SageMaker Pipelines, Azure ML pipelines, Airflow/MWAA), and CI/CD/CT with GitHub Actions or CodePipeline/CodeBuild/CodeDeploy, Gitflow or GitHub Flow, EventBridge retraining and automated tests. IaC tooling lives in provider folders and devops/.

articles.title: Compute for ML and GenAI: CPUs vs GPUs vs AI Accelerators, Sizing, Spot and Commitments
articles.scope: Compares CPUs, NVIDIA GPUs, Trainium, Inferentia and Azure ND/NC families by memory, interconnect and bandwidth, and instance families. Covers rightsizing (Inference Recommender, Compute Optimizer), Spot, Reserved and SageMaker Savings Plans vs Azure spot VMs and reservations, Azure ML compute targets, quotas and cost tagging; links cloud/*/compute and cost.

articles.title: Real-Time vs Batch vs Asynchronous vs Serverless Inference, and Safe Rollout
articles.scope: Compares modes by latency, cost, payload and scaling, including SageMaker Serverless limits (no GPUs, up to 6 GB, no Model Monitor, VPC or MME). Covers targets (endpoints, Kubernetes, ECS, Lambda), multi-model hosting, containers, edge, autoscaling metrics, and blue/green, canary, linear, shadow rollout and rollback.

articles.title: Monitoring Models in Production: Data Drift, Concept Drift and Retraining
articles.scope: Contrasts data, concept, prediction and attribution drift and training-serving skew; covers baselines, tests (JSD, PSI, Wasserstein, KS, chi-squared), late labels and retraining triggers. Uses Azure ML monitoring; notes SageMaker Model Monitor is closed to new customers (AWS points to MLflow plus Evidently with QuickSight and CloudWatch) and Azure ML's GenAI signal sits on retiring prompt flow.

articles.title: MLOps vs LLMOps (GenAIOps): What Changes for Foundation-Model Apps
articles.scope: Contrasts the lifecycles artifact by artifact (data vs prompts and indexes, training vs selection, accuracy vs open-ended quality, drift vs version churn, compute vs token cost) and lays out a GenAIOps lifecycle from Foundry environments to evaluation gates, monitoring and telemetry-driven tuning. Security baseline links to security/ai-security.

articles.title: CI/CD for GenAI Apps and Agents: Evaluation Gates, Prompt and Agent Versioning, Index Refresh and IaC
articles.scope: Versions prompts, agent definitions, tool schemas, deployments and index configs together, runs evaluations and security scans as gates, and promotes with rollback. Covers Foundry projects with GitHub Actions, Bicep and Azure CLI, CodePipeline equivalents, knowledge-base refresh, and ALM for data, custom models and Foundry Agent Service.

articles.title: Prompt Management: Prompts as Versioned, Tested Artifacts
articles.scope: Stores parameterized prompts in Git or a registry, compares variants with evals, gates changes with regression tests and approvals, and sets prompt-library guidelines. Contrasts Git plus Foundry evaluations with Bedrock Prompt Management and Amazon Bedrock Flows (exam wording: Prompt Flows) and MLflow; notes prompt flow retires 2027-04-20.

articles.title: Model Versions, Deprecations and Upgrades: Pinning, Auto-Upgrade Policies and Migration Testing
articles.scope: Foundry: Preview, GA, optional Legacy, Deprecated, Retired (HTTP 410), 18-month GA lifecycle (12 months for some publishers), versionUpgradeOption for Standard deployments, manual migration for provisioned. Bedrock: Active, Legacy (6 months or 45 days), EOL, no auto-migration. Covers pinning, replacement evaluation, prompt adaptation, regression testing and rollback.

articles.title: Operating RAG Indexes: Incremental Ingestion, Freshness, Deletions, Re-embedding and Index Health
articles.scope: Runs indexes as production assets: connectors, change detection (Cosmos DB change feed, indexer change tracking), scheduled refresh, tombstones, ACL sync, sharding, blue/green aliasing. Explains why an embedding-model change forces full re-embedding, and monitors ingestion quality, freshness, health and relevance.

articles.title: Self-Hosting and Serving LLMs: GPU Sizing, Continuous Batching, Quantized Serving, and Managed Compute vs Model APIs
articles.scope: Compares pay-per-token APIs with self-hosted or managed-compute serving. Covers vLLM, SGLang, TGI, Triton/TensorRT-LLM, KV-cache memory math, continuous batching, tensor parallelism, quantized weights and container packaging on SageMaker AI LMI, Bedrock Custom Model Import, Foundry managed compute (no deployment types), Container Apps, AKS, EKS and ECS GPUs.

articles.title: Latency vs Throughput for LLMs: TTFT, TPOT, TPM, Service Tiers and Provisioned Capacity
articles.scope: Explains prefill vs decode, TTFT, TPOT and end-to-end latency vs TPM/RPM, with a load-testing method. Compares Standard, Priority and Flex tiers on both clouds, Batch, Foundry PTU with spillover, Bedrock Provisioned Throughput (base or custom; none, 1 or 6 months) and Reserved tier (1 or 3 months, overflow), ramp-rate downgrades and HTTP 429 handling.

articles.title: Token Economics and GenAI Cost Optimization
articles.scope: Models cost per request and task (input, output, cached, cache-write, reasoning and embedding tokens, vector storage, evals, hosting) and applies levers: tiering and routing, compression, pruning, limits, caching, batch and Flex, provisioned capacity, attribution and anomaly detection. FinOps links to architecture/cost.

articles.title: Measuring GenAI Business Value: KPIs, ROI and TCO
articles.scope: Defines value metrics (productivity, efficiency, conversion, ARPU, CLV, task completion, satisfaction, cost per interaction), baselining and attribution, and builds ROI and TCO analyses with build-buy-extend choices and stakeholder reporting. Generic FinOps links to architecture/cost.

articles.title: Prompt Caching vs Semantic Caching vs Exact-Match Caching
articles.scope: Contrasts prefix caching, exact-match and semantic caching by reuse, hit conditions, cost and staleness. Dated specifics: Azure 1,024-token rule, prompt_cache_key, GPT-5.6+ breakpoints (30-minute minimum, billed writes), in_memory/24h retention earlier; Bedrock implicit and cachePoint caching (512-4,096 minimums, 4 checkpoints, 5-minute or 1-hour TTL, no batch). Redis semantic cache in C# and Python.

articles.title: GenAI Observability with OpenTelemetry GenAI Semantic Conventions
articles.scope: Instruments inference, retrieval, tool, agent and workflow calls with gen_ai.* spans and metrics (gen_ai.client.inference.duration, inference.usage.* counters incl. cache and reasoning tokens, server TTFT and TPOT, invoke_agent and execute_tool durations), pinning a semconv version. Builds dashboards and KQL for interpreting telemetry; compares Foundry tracing plus Application Insights with CloudWatch GenAI observability and Bedrock invocation logging.

articles.title: Troubleshooting GenAI Applications: A Symptom-to-Cause Cheat Sheet
articles.scope: Symptom-to-cause tables for context overflow, retrieval misses, regressions after upgrades, schema failures, HTTP 429 throttling, HTTP 400 unsupported tiers, HTTP 410 retired models, cache misses after prefix changes, token-accounting surprises (Converse inputTokens excludes cached tokens), tool-call errors and cost spikes, each with signal and fix.

articles.title: Open-Weight Models and Hugging Face: Hub, Transformers, PEFT, Licences and Cloud Catalogs
articles.scope: Wave 3. Definitions: open weights vs open source, using the OSI Open Source AI Definition. The Hugging Face Hub: model cards, safetensors, gated repos, revision pinning and the trust_remote_code risk. Libraries: Transformers pipelines and AutoModel, PEFT and LoRA adapters, and vLLM or TGI serving. Licences: Apache-2.0, MIT, community licences with usage thresholds, OpenRAIL-style acceptable-use terms, and how to record them. Cloud catalogs: Foundry Models (the Hugging Face collection, managed compute vs serverless), Bedrock Marketplace, Bedrock Custom Model Import and SageMaker JumpStart. Examples are in Python, with a C# path through ONNX Runtime GenAI and Foundry Local. It contrasts proprietary and open models for governance (AIGP 4.1.2) and links to assessing-ai-vendors-models-licenses and fine-tuning-methods.

terms.definition: Splitting live traffic between variants and comparing a predefined metric with a statistical test.
The fraction of all predictions that are correct, misleading when classes are imbalanced.
Retrieval where a model plans and iterates queries or tool calls and decides when it has enough evidence.
An app in which code fixes the sequence of model calls, tools and branches, unlike an agent, where the model picks the next step.
Hardware for training and inference matrix math, such as NVIDIA GPUs or AWS Trainium and Inferentia, far outperforming CPUs per dollar for deep learning.
Traditionally AI for IT operations, but Microsoft's AI-300 uses 'AI operations (AIOps)' for MLOps plus GenAIOps.
Systematic unfair differences in outputs or error rates across groups, often from unrepresentative data, skewed labels or proxy features.
Identifying observations that deviate markedly from expected patterns, usually without labels, for example with Random Cut Forest to flag fraud.
A metric for how directly and completely a response addresses the query, independent of source support.
The field of building systems that perform tasks associated with human intelligence, such as perception, language understanding, reasoning and decision-making.
Queuing requests to an endpoint and delivering each result later via notification or storage, suiting large payloads and long processing.
Automated search over algorithms, feature transforms and hyperparameters that returns ranked candidate models, as in Azure ML automated ML or AutoGluon.
AWS documentation for an AI service or model covering intended uses, limitations, responsible design choices and deployment practices.
AWS's eight dimensions: fairness, explainability, privacy and security, safety, controllability, veracity and robustness, governance, and transparency.
Computing the loss gradient for every weight by applying the chain rule backward through a network, so gradient descent can update weights.
Scoring large input sets as an asynchronous job, optimizing throughput and often discounted cost over latency.
Benchmark items appearing in training data, inflating scores without real capability.
A reference metric matching contextual embeddings of candidate and reference tokens, rewarding semantic rather than exact overlap.
Disparity measures computed on training data before training, such as CI and DPL, and on predictions after training, such as disparate impact.
The tension between error from overly simple assumptions (bias) and error from sensitivity to training data (variance), traded via complexity and regularization.
A reference-based metric scoring n-gram precision overlap with reference text, with a brevity penalty, originally for translation.
A lexical ranking function using term frequency, inverse document frequency and document length; the default full-text ranker in Azure AI Search and OpenSearch.
Routing traffic beyond reserved capacity to pay-as-you-go capacity instead of throttling, as in Foundry PTU spillover or Bedrock Reserved-tier overflow.
Losing previously learned capabilities when fine-tuning on new data, mitigated by mixing general data, lower learning rates or PEFT.
Converting category values into numbers, such as one-hot (a column per category), label (an integer per category) or binary encoding.
Asking a model to write intermediate reasoning before answering, often improving multi-step accuracy at the cost of output tokens.
Splitting documents into retrievable segments sized to balance retrieval precision against context completeness.
A skewed class distribution that biases training toward the majority class and makes accuracy misleading; mitigated by resampling, weights or synthetic data.
A supervised task that predicts a discrete category for each input, binary or multi-class.
An unsupervised task that groups similar data points without predefined labels, for example k-means customer segmentation.
A metric for whether a response is logically organized and reads as a connected whole, independent of grounding.
The branch of AI that interprets images and video, including classification, object detection, segmentation, OCR and captioning.
A change in the relationship between inputs and target, making the learned mapping wrong even with stable inputs.
A table of a classifier's true and false positives and negatives, from which accuracy, precision, recall and F1 derive.
Deciding which information enters the context window, in what order and format, within a token budget.
Retrieval metrics: context precision is the relevant share of retrieved content; context recall is the share of needed information it covers.
The maximum tokens a model attends to in one request, covering system prompt, history, retrieved content, tool definitions and output.
Resuming self-supervised training on large unlabeled domain corpora to adapt a model's knowledge and vocabulary.
Adding and removing sequences from the running GPU batch at every decode step to raise throughput, as vLLM and TensorRT-LLM do.
Automatically retraining and revalidating models on new data, schedules or drift triggers, the CT stage MLOps adds to CI/CD.
The cosine of the angle between two vectors, ignoring magnitude; on unit-length embeddings it equals the dot product.
Total model, retrieval, tool and hosting cost divided by completed interactions or tasks.
A model scoring query and document together in one pass, more accurate but slower than a bi-encoder that embeds each separately.
Training and validating repeatedly on different folds of the data to estimate generalization more reliably, especially on small datasets.
Enlarging or rebalancing training data with modified copies of real examples, such as rotated images, paraphrased text or added noise.
A change over time in input data distribution relative to training data, degrading performance even if the input-output relationship is unchanged.
Attaching ground-truth targets to raw data by people, models or both, for example with SageMaker Ground Truth or Azure ML data labeling.
Information unavailable at prediction time, such as target-derived features or test rows, leaking into training and inflating offline scores.

terms.term: Encoder-only vs decoder-only vs encoder-decoder models
terms.definition: Encoder-only models (BERT-style) build representations, decoder-only models (GPT-style) generate autoregressively, and encoder-decoder models (T5-style) map input to output sequences.
A subset of ML that uses multi-layer neural networks to learn representations directly from raw data such as text, images and audio.
A generative model that creates images, audio or video by iteratively denoising random noise under prompt guidance.
Projecting data onto fewer dimensions that keep most of its information, for example with PCA or autoencoders.
Preference alignment that fine-tunes directly on preferred and rejected response pairs, with no reward model or RL loop.
Training across devices by data parallelism (replicas on data shards) or model parallelism (the model split across devices).
Filtering retrieval to documents the caller may open, using synced ACL metadata or identity-aware connectors, so RAG never leaks content.
Halting training once a validation metric stops improving for a set number of steps, preventing overfitting and saving compute.
Running compiled or quantized models on devices near the data for low latency, offline operation or locality.
A dense numeric vector representing content so that semantically similar items lie close together, used for search, clustering and RAG.
A model that converts content into fixed-length vectors for similarity search instead of generating text.
Combining models by bagging, boosting or stacking to improve accuracy or robustness over any single model.
An epoch is one pass over the training data, a step processes one batch, and batch size is examples per step.
Grouping and inspecting failed cases to find systematic causes before changing prompts, retrieval or models.
A pipeline step blocking promotion of a prompt, model, index or agent version when metrics miss thresholds or regress.
An app-side cache keyed on a hash of the normalized request, safe but rarely hit by free-text queries.
Recording each run's parameters, metrics, code, data versions and artifacts for comparison and reproducibility.
The ability to describe why a model produced an output, via feature attributions such as SHAP, counterfactuals or source citations.
The harmonic mean of precision and recall, high only when both are high; also a token-overlap metric for generated answers.
Outcomes and error rates not systematically disadvantaging groups, measured with metrics such as demographic parity or equalized odds.

terms.term: Feature attribution drift and bias drift
terms.definition: Signals detecting production changes in which features drive predictions or in group-fairness metrics.
Creating, transforming and selecting model input variables from raw data through scaling, encoding, binning, log transforms and derived features.
Rescaling numeric features: normalization maps values into a fixed range such as 0 to 1, while standardization centers them on mean 0 with unit variance.
Choosing the subset of input variables that carries real signal, reducing overfitting, training time and model size.
A governed repository that serves the same feature logic offline for training and online for low-latency inference.
Including a few worked input-output examples so the model infers task and format.
Further training a pre-trained model's weights on task data to improve format, style, tool use or accuracy, not to add fresh knowledge.
A metric for whether a response is grammatical, natural and readable, independent of accuracy or relevance.
A large model pre-trained on broad data, usually self-supervised, that is adapted to many tasks through prompting, retrieval or fine-tuning.
Logit penalties against repetition: frequency scales with how often a token appeared, presence applies once it appeared at all.
Lexical retrieval over an inverted term index, usually BM25-ranked, matching exact words and codes but missing synonyms.
A capability where the model returns a structured request to invoke a defined tool, which the app executes and feeds back.
AI that produces new content such as text, code, images, audio or video by sampling from a learned model, rather than only classifying or predicting values.
A curated, versioned set of representative inputs with expected outputs or criteria for regression-testing an app.
An ensemble that builds shallow trees sequentially, each fitting the remaining errors; XGBoost, LightGBM and CatBoost are common implementations.
An optimizer that repeatedly moves parameters a small step against the loss gradient; SGD and Adam are common variants.
RAG that extracts entities and relationships into a knowledge graph and traverses or summarizes it to answer multi-hop and corpus-wide questions.
Always choosing the most probable next token, the limiting case of temperature 0, exploring no alternatives.
A metric for how fully a response's claims are supported by the provided context, regardless of whether it answers the question.
Anchoring responses in supplied, verifiable data such as retrieved documents or tool results rather than parametric memory.
Fluent, plausible output that is wrong, unsupported by provided sources or invented, such as a fake citation.
Indexing small child chunks for precise matching but returning their larger parent chunks for context.
People rating or comparing outputs against guidelines, slower than automated metrics but the reference for calibrating them.
Designing systems so people review, approve or correct outputs at defined points, overseeing high-risk decisions.
Running full-text and vector queries together and fusing ranked results, often with RRF, to combine exact matching with semantic recall.
A setting fixed before training, such as learning rate, batch size or tree depth, unlike the weights the model learns from data.
Searching hyperparameter values by grid, random or Bayesian search to optimize a validation metric, as SageMaker AMT and Azure ML sweep jobs do.
A model performing a new task from instructions and examples in the prompt at inference time, with no weight change.
Updating an index by processing only new, changed or deleted source documents detected through change tracking instead of rebuilding.
Using a trained model to produce predictions or generated content for new inputs without changing its parameters.
A per-request processing tier on shared capacity trading latency and availability for price, set via service_tier values such as priority, default and flex.
Automating document workflows by combining OCR, layout, classification and field extraction into structured data with confidence scores for review.
How far a model's mechanics are understandable by construction, as with linear models and shallow trees.
A setting that guarantees syntactically valid JSON but enforces no particular schema.
Training a smaller student model to reproduce a larger teacher's outputs, often on teacher-generated data, for near-teacher quality at lower cost.
A graph of entities and typed relationships, stored in a graph database such as Amazon Neptune, supporting multi-hop traversal.
Stored attention keys and values for processed tokens that let a transformer generate without recomputing the prefix; prompt caching builds on it.
Labeled data pairs each example with a known target; unlabeled data has inputs only and supports unsupervised or self-supervised learning.
A transformer foundation model trained on large text corpora to predict the next token, enabling instruction following, coding and tool calling.
Detecting document structure such as paragraphs, headings, tables, selection marks and reading order so extracted text keeps its meaning.
The hyperparameter that sets each update's step size; too high diverges, too low converges slowly or stalls.
Using a capable LLM with a rubric to score or compare outputs, scalable but prone to position, verbosity and self-preference bias.
A standardized public task suite for comparing model capabilities, not a substitute for evaluating your own application.
The same prompt producing different outputs across calls due to sampling and serving-side batching and floating-point effects, even at temperature 0.
Operations for foundation-model apps: prompt and model versioning, evaluation, deployment, cost, quota and latency management, safety monitoring and tracing.
Per-token log-probabilities some APIs return, used to estimate confidence, calibrate classifications and flag uncertain answers.
Placing whole documents in a large context window instead of retrieving chunks; cache-augmented generation preloads and caches that context.
A PEFT method that trains small low-rank adapter matrices on a frozen base model; QLoRA applies it to a quantized base.
The quantity training minimizes, measuring the gap between predictions and targets, such as cross-entropy or mean squared error.
The tendency of LLMs to use information at the start and end of a long context more reliably than in the middle.
A branch of AI in which systems learn patterns from data to make predictions or decisions instead of following explicitly programmed rules.
Automatically translating text or speech between languages with a dedicated translation model or by prompting an LLM.
Embeddings trained so truncated prefixes remain useful, letting you store fewer dimensions without re-embedding.
A cap on generated tokens that bounds cost and latency but can truncate answers; on many reasoning models it includes hidden reasoning tokens.
The average over queries of 1 divided by the rank of the first relevant result.
Restricting vector search with attribute conditions applied before the ANN scan or to its results, the latter risking too few matches.
Microsoft's six principles (fairness, reliability and safety, privacy and security, inclusiveness, transparency, accountability), operationalized by its Responsible AI Standard.
An architecture whose router sends each token to a few expert sub-networks, so only part of the parameters is active per token.
The artifact training produces, learned parameters plus structure that map inputs to outputs, as distinct from the algorithm that learned them.
An orchestrated, versioned DAG of preparation, training, evaluation and registration steps, such as SageMaker Pipelines or Azure ML pipelines.
An open-source platform for experiment tracking, model packaging and registry, built into Azure ML and offered managed on SageMaker AI.
Applying DevOps to the ML lifecycle: versioned data and code, tracking, pipelines, registry, deployment, monitoring and retraining.
A document describing a model's intended use, training data, evaluation results, limitations and ethical considerations.
Training reaching a stable loss minimum; failures include divergence, vanishing or exploding gradients and plateaus, diagnosed with tools like SageMaker Debugger.
A versioned catalog of models with metadata, lineage and stages that gates deployment and supports rollback and audit.
Choosing which model serves each request by rules, classifier or trained router, balancing quality, cost and latency with cascades and fallback.
Fixing a deployment to a model version and controlling upgrades, such as Foundry versionUpgradeOption or dated Bedrock model IDs, so changes follow regression tests.
One endpoint hosting many models on shared infrastructure, loading each on demand to cut cost at cold-load latency.
A model that accepts or produces more than one modality, such as text, images, audio and video.
Identifying and classifying mentions of people, organizations, places, dates and amounts in text.
The branch of AI that analyzes, understands and generates human language, including entity recognition, sentiment, summarization and translation.
A ranking metric using graded relevance discounted by position and normalized against the ideal ordering.
Text describing what a generator should avoid, mostly used with image models.
A model of layered weighted nodes with non-linear activations, trained by backpropagation and gradient descent.
Locating each object in an image or frame with a bounding box and label, unlike classification, which labels the whole image.
Scoring a model or app against a fixed dataset before release, making comparisons repeatable and enabling CI gates.
Measuring quality on live or sampled production traffic via feedback, experiments and automated evaluators on traces.
AI released with freedoms to use, study, modify and share; the OSI definition also requires code and detailed training-data information, which many open-weight models lack.
A model whose weights are downloadable for self-hosting under a license that may restrict use, not necessarily with training data or code.
Arize-led OpenTelemetry-based conventions and instrumentation for LLM and agent tracing that overlap with but differ from OTel gen_ai.*.
Development-status OTel conventions, now in open-telemetry/semantic-conventions-genai, for inference, retrieval, tool, agent and workflow telemetry using gen_ai.* attributes.
Extracting machine-readable text from images or scanned documents, the first step before layout analysis and field extraction.
When a model learns noise in its training data, scoring well there but generalizing poorly to unseen data.
Training only a small set of added parameters, such as LoRA adapters, while base weights stay frozen.
Calling a provider-hosted model on shared capacity billed per token, such as Foundry Global Standard deployments or Bedrock on-demand inference.
A reference score from a simple model, heuristic or current production model that a candidate must beat, and the reference distribution for drift checks.
The initial compute-intensive training of a foundation model on massive unlabeled data with a self-supervised objective.
The fraction of positive predictions that are truly positive, TP / (TP + FP), key when false positives are costly.
The fraction of the top k retrieved results that are relevant.
A shift in the distribution of model outputs versus validation or recent data, signaling problems before labels arrive.
Prefill processes the whole prompt in parallel and builds the KV cache, setting TTFT; decode then generates tokens one at a time, setting TPOT.
Provider reuse of computed state for an identical prompt prefix, cutting latency and discounting cached input, automatically or at explicit breakpoints.
Splitting a task into sequential model calls where each output feeds the next prompt, with validation between steps.
Shortening prompts by summarizing history, removing redundancy or learned compressors, cutting tokens while keeping needed information.
Designing instructions, context, examples and output specifications to get reliable responses without changing model weights.
Storing prompts as versioned, parameterized, reviewed artifacts with variants and evaluation results, decoupled from code.
A reusable prompt with named placeholders filled at run time, separating fixed instructions from variable input.
Dedicated model capacity billed by time or reserved TPM rather than tokens used, such as Foundry PTUs or Bedrock Provisioned Throughput and Reserved tier.
Removing weights, neurons, heads or layers that contribute little, to shrink a model and speed inference, usually followed by brief retraining.
Lowering weight and activation precision, for example 16-bit to 8- or 4-bit, to cut memory and speed inference at some quality risk.
Transforming a query before retrieval by rephrasing, expanding, decomposing or embedding a hypothetical answer to improve recall.
Serving predictions synchronously from an always-on endpoint with low per-request latency.
A setting that bounds the hidden reasoning tokens a reasoning model spends before answering; those tokens count toward output limits and are billed as output.
A model trained to spend extra inference-time compute on hidden reasoning before answering, improving multi-step tasks at higher latency and cost.
The fraction of actual positives correctly found, TP / (TP + FN), key when missing a positive is costly.
The fraction of all relevant documents appearing in the top k results.
Merging ranked lists by summing 1/(k + rank) per document, avoiding comparison of incompatible raw scores.
A model that ranks items for each user from behavioral and content signals using collaborative filtering, factorization machines or embeddings.
A model or second model reviewing a draft against criteria and revising it, trading extra calls for quality.
A supervised task that predicts a continuous value, such as a price, scored with error metrics like MAE or RMSE.
Techniques such as L1 and L2 penalties and dropout that penalize complexity or inject noise during training to reduce overfitting.
Fine-tuning where a grader or reward function, such as a Foundry grader or Bedrock Lambda reward function, scores sampled responses for checkable tasks.
A paradigm in which an agent learns a policy by acting in an environment and maximizing cumulative reward.
A second stage in which a costlier model, usually a cross-encoder, re-scores top first-stage candidates to raise precision.
Designing and operating AI to maximize benefit while managing unfairness, unsafe output, privacy loss and lack of transparency or accountability.
Retrieving relevant external content at query time and adding it to the prompt so the model answers from current or private data.
A model exploiting flaws in its reward model or grader to raise its score without genuinely improving.
A model trained on preference rankings to score responses, used as the optimization target in RLHF.
Alignment that trains a reward model on human preferences, then optimizes the LLM against it with reinforcement learning.
The ROC curve plots true- vs false-positive rate across thresholds; its area (AUC) summarizes ranking quality independent of any threshold.
Regression error metrics: MAE averages absolute errors, while RMSE squares errors first and so penalizes large errors more.
Recall-oriented reference metrics, common for summarization, measuring n-gram or longest-common-subsequence overlap.
Selection bias comes from unrepresentative sampling; measurement bias from systematically wrong features or labels.
The transformer mechanism in which each token weighs its relevance to every other token in context to build context-aware representations.
Learning from labels derived from the data itself, such as predicting the next or a masked token, which is how foundation models are pre-trained.
An app-side cache returning a stored response, skipping the model, when a new query's embedding is close to a previous one.
Retrieval by meaning, usually built on vector search; Azure AI Search's 'semantic ranker' is instead a second-stage reranker.
Classifying the opinion or tone in text as positive, negative, neutral or mixed, at document, sentence or aspect level.
Serving your own model on on-demand compute that scales to zero, billed by compute time, with cold starts and limits; SageMaker's has no GPUs and at most 6 GB.
Copying production traffic to a candidate whose outputs are logged and compared but never returned to users.
SHapley Additive exPlanations, attributing a prediction to features with game-theory Shapley values, used by tools such as SageMaker Clarify.
A language model with comparatively few parameters, roughly hundreds of millions to about 15 billion with no formal threshold, trading breadth for cost, latency and edge deployment.
Retrieval with sparse vocabulary-sized term-weight vectors, lexical like BM25 or learned by a neural model, instead of dense embeddings.
A small draft model proposes tokens the large model verifies in one pass, keeping the large model's output distribution while generating faster.
A model that takes audio in and returns audio out directly, cutting latency and preserving tone versus a cascaded STT-LLM-TTS pipeline.
Converting spoken audio into a text transcript.
A string that ends generation as soon as the model produces it.
Data in a fixed schema of rows and typed columns, such as tables and time series, that models can consume directly as features.
Constraining output to a supplied JSON Schema, usually via constrained decoding, so responses always parse.
Fine-tuning on labeled prompt-response pairs that demonstrate desired behavior.
Training on labeled examples, each input paired with a known output, so the model predicts labels for new inputs, as in classification and regression.
Training or evaluation data generated by models or programs to supplement scarce data, rebalance classes, distill models or build test sets.
Privileged-role instructions that set persona, rules, constraints and output format for a whole conversation.
The share of tasks or sessions in which an assistant or agent achieves the user's goal.
A sampling parameter that rescales token probabilities; lower is more deterministic, higher more varied.
Splitting individual weight matrices across GPUs so each computes part of every layer, for models too large or slow for one device.
Converting text into synthesized speech with selectable voices and optional SSML control of pronunciation and prosody.
Translating a question into a SQL query whose execution returns an exact, auditable answer instead of a generated one.
Average time between output tokens during decode, recorded as gen_ai.server.time_per_output_token.
Predicting future values of a time-ordered series from its history and covariates, for example demand forecasting with DeepAR.
Latency until the first output token arrives, dominated by queuing and prefill; recorded as gen_ai.server.time_to_first_token.
The unit of text a model reads and generates, such as a word piece or byte sequence, in which context limits, quotas and pricing are counted.
Billing per input and output token, where output usually costs more, cached input less, some models bill cache writes, and reasoning bills as output.
Splitting text into a model's tokens with a tokenizer such as BPE or SentencePiece, so the same text yields different counts on different models.
A throughput quota on tokens per minute, enforced alongside requests per minute; exceeding either returns HTTP 429.
Whether an agent picked the right tools with correct arguments in a sensible order.
Sampling only from the k most probable next tokens at each step.
Sampling only from the smallest token set whose cumulative probability reaches p, discarding the long tail.
A mismatch between feature computation at training and serving time that degrades a model from its first day.
Partitioning data into a training set that fits parameters, a validation set for tuning and model choice, and a held-out test set for a final unbiased estimate.
Scoring an agent's sequence of steps and tool calls against an expected path or rubric, not just its final answer.
Reusing a model trained on one task as the starting point for a related task, needing less data and compute; fine-tuning is its commonest form.
A self-attention architecture that processes tokens in parallel during training and prefill, then generates autoregressively one token at a time; it underlies modern LLMs.
Microsoft documentation for an AI service explaining capabilities, intended uses, limitations and responsible deployment choices.
When a model is too simple or undertrained to capture the pattern, performing poorly on both training and unseen data.
Data without a predefined schema, such as text, images, audio and video, that needs parsing, OCR or embedding before most models can use it.
Training on unlabeled data to discover structure such as clusters, associations, compact representations or anomalies.
The data structure inside a store, such as flat, HNSW, IVF or DiskANN, that speeds nearest-neighbor search.
Retrieving items whose embeddings are nearest the query embedding, matching meaning rather than exact terms.
A multimodal model that takes images or video frames plus text and produces text, for captioning, visual Q&A and document understanding.
Speech-recognition accuracy: substitutions, deletions and insertions divided by the number of reference words.
Asking a model to do a task from instructions alone, with no worked examples.

pairs.difference: Deep learning learns its own features with multi-layer networks; classic ML relies on engineered features and suits smaller tabular data.
A traditional model is trained for one task on your labels and is cheap and explainable; a foundation model is pre-trained broadly and adapted, trading explainability and compute for flexibility.
The algorithm is the learning procedure; the model is the trained artifact it produces from specific data.
Supervised learning predicts known labels; unsupervised learning finds structure with no ground truth to score against.
Classification predicts a class and is scored by precision, recall or F1; regression predicts a number and is scored by MAE or RMSE.
Training updates weights and is compute-heavy and periodic; inference serves from fixed weights and dominates production cost and latency.
Overfitting shows high training but low validation scores; underfitting shows low scores on both.
Precision penalizes false positives; recall penalizes false negatives.
On imbalanced data a majority-class guesser scores high accuracy but near-zero F1, since F1 ignores true negatives.
Normalization rescales into a fixed range and is outlier-sensitive; standardization centers on mean 0 with unit variance.
Bagging trains models in parallel on resamples to cut variance; boosting trains them sequentially, each correcting the last, to cut bias.
Data parallelism replicates a model that fits on one device and splits data; model parallelism splits the model itself when it does not fit.
Augmentation perturbs real examples so labels carry over; synthetic data is generated from scratch and must be validated for realism and leakage.
Selection keeps interpretable original columns; reduction such as PCA creates new combined dimensions that no longer map to originals.
Loss is the differentiable quantity training minimizes; the metric is what the business cares about and may not align with the loss.
Data drift changes the input distribution; concept drift changes the input-to-target relationship, even with unchanged inputs.
Drift appears over time after deployment; skew exists from day one because features are computed differently, and is fixed in the pipeline, not by retraining.
Interpretable models are understandable by construction; explainability adds post-hoc explanations to models that are not.
Encoders read input bidirectionally for classification and embeddings; decoders generate left to right, which is why chat LLMs are decoder-only.
A token is a discrete text unit that is read, generated and billed; an embedding is a dense vector representing meaning.
Temperature reshapes the whole distribution while top-p truncates it to a nucleus; adjust one, not both.
Temperature 0 approximates greedy decoding but serving-side batching and floating-point effects still cause variation.
The window caps input plus output per request; max output tokens caps generation only, often including hidden reasoning.
CoT prompts any model to write steps; a reasoning model is trained to reason in hidden tokens, so explicit CoT adds little.
Zero-shot relies on instructions; few-shot adds examples that pin format and edge cases at extra input-token cost.
Prompt engineering crafts instructions; context engineering governs everything else in the window and its ordering under a budget.
JSON mode guarantees valid JSON; structured outputs guarantee conformance to a specific schema.
Structured outputs shape the final answer; function calling emits arguments for a tool the app runs and feeds back.
In a workflow code fixes the steps, so it is predictable and testable; an agent lets the model choose steps, handling open tasks at the cost of predictability and spend.
RAG injects fresh, citable knowledge at query time; fine-tuning changes weights for behavior and format, and keeps facts poorly fresh.
Long context is simple but costly per call and prone to lost-in-the-middle; RAG retrieves only relevant chunks and scales to large access-controlled corpora.
Vector RAG retrieves similar passages for explanations; text-to-SQL executes a query for exact counts, sums and lookups that retrieval cannot compute.
Vector search matches meaning but can miss identifiers; BM25 matches exact terms but misses synonyms; hybrid combines both.
Hybrid search widens first-stage recall by fusing keyword and vector results; reranking re-scores top candidates in a second stage for precision.
Semantic search is meaning-based first-stage retrieval; Azure AI Search's semantic ranker is a second-stage reranker over retrieved results.
The database is the store and service; the index is one ANN structure inside it, and a store can hold several.
HNSW gives high recall at low latency but uses more memory; IVF is leaner but recall depends on partitions probed.
Pre-filtering constrains the scan and still returns k matches; post-filtering trims top-k afterwards and can return few or none.
Vector RAG suits local fact lookup; GraphRAG answers multi-hop and corpus-wide questions at higher indexing and upkeep cost.
Grounding is the technique of supplying source data; groundedness is the metric for how well claims are supported by it.
Groundedness asks whether claims are supported; relevance asks whether the question is answered, so an answer can be grounded yet irrelevant.
Fine-tuning uses labeled examples to shape behavior; continued pre-training runs self-supervised training on unlabeled domain text to shift knowledge.
SFT imitates demonstrations; RFT needs only prompts and a grader, suits checkable tasks and risks reward hacking.
RLHF trains a reward model and runs RL; DPO optimizes directly on preference pairs, simpler and more stable but offline.
A judge is a prompted model scoring for evaluation; a reward model is trained on preferences as an RLHF optimization target.
Distillation trains a different smaller model; quantization keeps the model and lowers its numeric precision.
Model quantization shrinks weights to speed inference; vector quantization compresses stored embeddings, trading retrieval recall.
Open-weight means downloadable weights under some license; OSI open-source AI also requires code, training-data information and full freedoms.
Offline is repeatable scoring on a fixed set before release; online measures real traffic with more noise and user risk.
Reference metrics count overlap and penalize valid paraphrases; judges assess meaning by rubric but need calibration to human labels.
HITL puts people inside the production flow; human evaluation scores samples offline to calibrate metrics.
A/B exposes users to variants and measures outcomes; shadow mirrors traffic without returning outputs, so it cannot measure user impact.
Precision@k matters when the context budget is small; recall@k matters when a missed fact causes a wrong answer.
Serverless inference hosts your own model on on-demand compute with cold starts and hardware limits; a pay-per-token API serves a provider model per token with nothing to deploy.
Batch scores a whole dataset as one job; async queues individual requests to an endpoint and returns each when ready.
Continuous batching is a GPU serving technique interleaving live requests; batch inference is an offline job type.
Provisioned capacity is reserved and paid by time; priority pays a per-token premium on shared capacity and can be downgraded under ramps or peaks.
Spillover keeps the model and moves excess traffic to pay-as-you-go capacity; fallback switches model or Region and can change quality.
Prompt caching reuses a provider-side prefix and the model still runs; semantic caching skips the model for similar queries but risks wrong answers.
Exact-match is safe but rarely hits free text; semantic hits far more often but may answer a subtly different question.
TTFT is set by prefill and queuing; TPOT by decode speed; caching targets the first and speculative decoding the second.
TTFT is one user's responsiveness; throughput is aggregate capacity, and aggressive batching can raise throughput while hurting TTFT.
MoE routes tokens among sub-networks inside one model; model routing picks which separate model serves each request.
MLOps centers on training, retraining and drift for models you build; LLMOps on prompts, retrieval, open-ended evaluation, token cost and safety for models you consume.
The established meaning applies ML to IT operations; AI-300 uses AIOps for MLOps plus GenAIOps, so read the context.
OCR turns pixels into text; IDP adds layout, classification, field extraction, confidence and review for trustworthy structured data.
A purpose-built API is cheaper per record, deterministic and documented; an LLM is more flexible but costlier, variable and needs its own evaluation.
A cascade is modular and auditable but adds latency and loses tone; a native speech model is faster and more natural but harder to inspect and constrain.

- MLA-C01 v1.0 PDF is still published: 28/26/22/24, 50+15 questions, pass 720; quantizing models is out of scope. - Foundry: deployment types apply only to the Serverless API option, not managed compute. Batch is 50% off with a 24-hour target. Developer is for evaluating fine-tuned models only: 24-hour lifetime, no SLA or residency. Instant access (preview) needs no deployment. Priority and Flex are request-level service_tier choices: Priority runs on GlobalStandard and US DataZoneStandard and is downgraded on ramps over 50% TPM in under 15 minutes; Flex (preview) is 50% off, GlobalStandard only, returns 429 when capacity is unavailable and 400 for unsupported models, with no fallback. Gateways can set the x-ms-service-tier header. PTU spillover uses spilloverDeploymentName or the x-ms-spillover-deployment header.
- Foundry lifecycle: Preview, GA, Legacy (optional), Deprecated, Retired (410). GA lasts 18 months (12 for Anthropic, DeepSeek, Fireworks and Mistral AI). versionUpgradeOption controls upgrades; provisioned deployments are never auto-upgraded.
- Foundry prompt caching: 1,024-token minimum; GPT-5.6+ adds breakpoints, a 30-minute TTL and billed cache writes; PTU-M has no breakpoints.
- Foundry model router: 2025-11-18 is updated in place; Claude must be deployed separately; context is limited by the smallest underlying model; routing decisions use text only.
- Foundry fine-tuning: managed fine-tuning vs interactive training (preview), both on Foundry-managed infrastructure; managed compute is now a LoRA serving option, so the critique's 'own VMs' framing applies only to classic hub projects.
- Azure AI Search agentic retrieval: REST 2026-04-01 is GA (minimal retrieval); 2026-08-01-preview adds query planning; knowledge bases expose an MCP endpoint.
- Prompt flow retires 2027-04-20. Azure ML monitoring signals and statistics confirmed. Content Understanding: GA API 2025-11-01. The Azure SQL vector type is GA.
- Bedrock: service tiers are Reserved (1 or 3 months, minimum 100k input / 10k output TPM, overflows to Standard, 99.5% target), Priority, Standard ('default') and Flex. Provisioned Throughput covers base or custom models with no commitment, 1-month or 6-month terms; supported custom models can also use on-demand deployment.
- Bedrock lifecycle (models launched from 2026-09-07): Active, Legacy (6 months or 45 days), EOL, with no auto-migration.
- Bedrock customization: SFT, RFT and distillation only; no CPT or DPO.
- Bedrock prompt caching: 512-4,096 token minimums, 4 checkpoints, TTL of 5 minutes, 1 hour on Claude or 30 minutes on GPT-5.6+, no batch; Responses API runs on bedrock-runtime and bedrock-mantle.
- Bedrock Intelligent Prompt Routing: two models of one family, English-optimized. GraphRAG limits confirmed. AgentCore Evaluations modes confirmed; the product is named Bedrock Flows.
- SageMaker Serverless exclusions confirmed. SageMaker Model Monitor is closed to new customers.
- OTel: conventions are in open-telemetry/semantic-conventions-genai (Development). Inference calls use gen_ai.client.inference.duration, not gen_ai.client.operation.duration. Token usage uses gen_ai.client.inference.usage.* counters. Server metrics are time_to_first_token and time_per_output_token, and gen_ai.provider.name is required on them.
